findings.analysis: This overview repeats inline:4287738622; there is no separate defect. Not reproducible on the frozen repository's pinned Gradle 9.8.1. TestSuiteExecutionsPlugin applies jvm-test-suite before attaching its configureEach callback (TestSuiteExecutions.kt:18-21). Gradle 9.8.1 JvmTestSuitePlugin.apply already installs testing.suites.withType(JvmTestSuite).all(...), and its callback also installs targets.all(...). Consequently register<JvmTestSuite>("integrationTest") executes the suite configuration without an explicit provider.get(), and the existing code adds both default and variant tasks to check (TestSuiteExecutions.kt:56-73). An investigation-only ProjectBuilder regression resolved check dependencies without first realizing the named suite or any Test tasks and passed unchanged; it observed test, integrationTest, and integrationTestExperimental. A separate evaluated Kotlin DSL build using the exact register<JvmTestSuite> form also included both named-suite tasks in check --dry-run, with an assertion that no Test task was realized during configuration. The existing seven convention tests passed after removing the investigation-only test. Changing configureEach to all would not fix a supported failure on this frozen build.

findings.body:
### 🟡 Changes recommended Lazily registered named suites can leave their executions silently disconnected from `check`.
1 open finding - [Named test suite remains unrealized, causing check to skip tests](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20625#discussion_r4287738622) · New
🧠 **Review effort:** Balanced

[Build] A named suite declared with `register<JvmTestSuite>("integrationTest") { executions { ... } }` can remain unrealized when running `check`: this lazy callback does not realize it, and its `check` dependencies are only added inside the suite's configuration. Without another reference that realizes the suite, `check` silently skips both its default execution and variants. The named-suite test hides this by calling `.get()` first. Eagerly configure suite registrations here, and add a regression that resolves `check` dependencies without first realizing the named suite or its tasks.

Related to https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/issues/19792

Proposes suite-owned test executions to reduce variant boilerplate without copying configured `Test` tasks. This proof of concept adds reusable infrastructure and migrates only gRPC javaagent, preserving its default execution and all four variants.

```kotlin
executions {
  configureEach {
    jvmArgs("-Djava.net.preferIPv4Stack=true")
  }
  register("Experimental") {
    telemetryConfig("otel.instrumentation.grpc.experimental-span-attributes", "true")
  }
}
```

- **Ownership:** `JvmTestSuite` retains compilation and dependencies. Executions reuse its output and runtime classpath and join `check` automatically.
- **Configuration:** Common settings precede variant settings regardless of declaration order. Each task receives shared conventions independently, preserving JVM argument providers without duplication.
- **Telemetry:** `telemetryConfig` composes JVM properties and metadata conditions; variant values override common values. Ordinary JVM properties remain unlabeled.
- **Scope:** Preserves gRPC task names, request-metadata settings, classpath filtering, dependency constraints, and latest-dependency/denyUnsafe behavior. Adds focused infrastructure coverage; no other instrumentation migrations or general test matrix.
metadata.title: Prototype suite-owned Gradle test executions with gRPC
